title: Atomic snippet orbits: composable onboarding cards for ephemeral keys, streaming, and tool-calls
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Objective: Produce a compact, composable set of UI/code-card assets ("atomic snippet orbits") to be used across API/SDK onboarding docs and the Console quickstart. Each card is self-contained and can be tiled in documentation, tutorials, or the in-product first-run carousel.

Background: Current onboarding visuals are a mix of full-screen walkthroughs and long tutorial pages. We need a set of bite-sized, remixable cards that demonstrate three core flows: ephemeral key provisioning and rotation, streaming responses (server-sent events / streaming SDK), and tool-calling/stateful tool executions with simple visual state transitions. Cards must be language-agnostic (JS/Python snippets), responsive, and support a small animated state to show async behavior.

Scope: Deliver a design kit with 12 unique cards (4 per flow), 3 vector illustrations for each card type (idle, loading/streaming, success/fallback), and two short GIF prototypes demonstrating tiled behaviour in docs and a Console-side first-run carousel. Provide Figma components, export-ready PNG/SVG assets, and Storybook-ready React snippets (hand-off with dev notes).

Success metrics: cards adopted in at least 3 top-level docs (API Quickstart, SDK Guide, Console First Run) and reduce time-to-first-success metric in onboarding funnel by 10% (measured by analytics event quickstart.finish).

Design constraints and tradeoffs: Keep the visual language consistent with Redwood brand but lower fidelity than full product mockups to allow rapid translations. Avoid showing sensitive flows (real keys) — use ephemeral placeholders and emphasize "copy ephemeral key" action. For streaming, prefer a micro-activity indicator and truncated tokenized output rather than full transcript to reduce cognitive load. Tool-call cards need to illustrate state (pending -> success/failure) with a simplified stepper rather than full logs.

Deliverables: Figma file (components + prototypes), exportable asset folder, handoff doc with copy strings and accessibility notes, and a small QA checklist for developers implementing in Storybook/Docs.
acceptance_criteria: 12 card designs exported as PNG and SVG (4 per flow)
Figma components with variants for idle/loading/success/failure
Two prototype GIFs (docs carousel and console first-run) showing animated streaming and tool-call transitions
Storybook-ready code examples for JS and Python with copyable snippets
Handoff doc with copy, alt text, and localization notes
Design reviewed and approved by PM and Design Lead
comments: 2026-02-18: Ticket created — initial brief attached. Assigned to Diego for concept sketches. Aisha to align with PM on priority flows.

2026-02-22: Reviewed with PM (Priya Raman). Feedback: make ephemeral key action more discoverable and add a gentle warning copy for rotation. Move streaming examples to show partial output commits.

2026-02-24: Design review with Engineering representatives. Eng raised constraints about GIF sizes in docs and recommended providing a static fallback sprite plus one compressed GIF per flow. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-02-26: Prototype GIFs exported. Uploaded to Drive and Storybook stub created. Opened PR for docs inclusion: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412. PM approved visuals pending a short accessibility review.

2026-02-27: Accessibility review notes: ensure 3:1 contrast on microtext, include aria-hidden for decorative SVGs, and provide concise alt text. Security flagged to ensure no live key material in assets. Marking security_review_required=true.
2026-02-27: Next steps: finalize export assets, add localization-ready copy tokens, handoff to ENG for Storybook integration and docs PR update. Due date set to 2026-03-10.
